key_insight: EngramRAG turns agent memory into an adaptive, usage-weighted graph that learns which facts to keep, which links to strengthen, and which obsolete states to suppress across long conversations.
engineering_relevance: For autonomous engineering agents, this architecture improves multi-hop retrieval and long-term state consistency, which are critical for reliable decision support, design workflows, and persistent personas.
method: Usage-Modulated Personalized PageRank (U-PPR) boosts frequently useful entities into stable high-centrality hubs.
Consolidation-Activated Topology Decay (CATD) preserves load-bearing memories based on graph importance rather than simple recency.
SUPERSEDES and hybrid RRF retrieval combine dense vectors, BM25, and graph signals to reduce stale or conflicting memory.
evidence_signal: On LoCoMo’s 1,982 QA pairs, EngramRAG improved Recall@5 to 53.21% versus 38.29% for dense RAG and raised MRR to 0.4203, while eliminating split-brain hallucinations in mutation tests.
watch_item: The system adds algorithmic and operational complexity, so real-world deployment must manage tuning, latency stability, and robustness of graph maintenance at scale.
paper_title: EngramRAG: Dynamic Usage-Weighted Topology and Synaptic Consolidation for Multi-Hop Agentic Memory
